APEX-Agents

paper.arxiv.2601.14242

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2601.14242v3. Expert world/task/rubric evaluation and judge self-preference caveat establish task/evaluation methods. Estimated/actual baselining-time arithmetic discrepancy remains; no new family credit. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Worlds are controlled and web search is disabled; the judge is also a leaderboard model, creating a self-preference risk, and aggregate successful-trajectory tool-use associations do not control for task difficulty or agent approach.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

APEX-Agents grades each human-authored rubric criterion independently with Gemini 3 Flash and defines task success as satisfying all criteria; Pass@1 averages eight runs per task, while Pass@8 and Pass^8 measure any-attempt success and all-attempt consistency.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The benchmark includes 480 tasks split equally among investment banking, law and management consulting across 33 worlds; 256 experts from Mercor’s marketplace create and review worlds, tasks, gold outputs and rubrics, and independent experts baseline 96 tasks.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Table 3 reports Pass@1 of 24.0% for Gemini 3 Flash and 23.0% for GPT-5.2, with 95% task-bootstrap intervals 20.7–27.3 and 19.8–26.2; the paper’s corrected paired tests do not find their difference significant.
